participants: Chris Eichenlaub, Jim Guilfoyle, Rebecca Blaschak, Dan Giles, Mary Kuhn, Ed Maddox, Neda Newnam, Jen Edwards, Tyler Schulmeister (and 83 community residents)
content:
The SCCA held a Special Community Benefits District (SCBD) Information Meeting and Annual Meeting at the Shipley’s Choice Swim Club. President Chris Eichenlaub called the meeting to order at 7:03 p.m. with all nine Board members present (Chris Eichenlaub, Jim Guilfoyle, Rebecca Blaschak, Dan Giles, Mary Kuhn, Ed Maddox, Neda Newnam, Jen Edwards, and Tyler Schulmeister), along with 69 residents attending in person and 14 via livestream.

President Chris Eichenlaub presented an overview of the proposed Special Community Benefits District (SCBD). The presentation addressed SCCA's nonprofit organizational status and governing documents, noting a legal opinion that SCCA is not subject to Maryland Title 11B (the Maryland Homeowners Association Act), holding a 2026 Certificate of Good Standing from the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation, and affirming that the 1980 Articles of Incorporation and Bylaws apply to both Sections 1 and 2. He also clarified that rumors of Anne Arundel County taking over SCCA are entirely without merit, as the Board is fully staffed. The Board highlighted recent communication upgrades, including website improvements, a community discussion forum, enhanced email outreach, and plans for quarterly virtual meetings.

The presentation reviewed voluntary dues collection trends: across 283 homes in Sections 1 and 2, approximately 68% of households paid the $75 voluntary dues in 2025, yielding about $17,500 and constraining funds for rising community costs like tree removal and insurance. In response, the Board voted in December 2025 to pursue an SCBD (similar to neighboring communities like Chartwell), with the County legal office affirming eligibility in July 2026. Under the proposal, Anne Arundel County would collect the assessment via property tax bills, charge a 5% administrative fee, and disburse funds to SCCA. Formation requires petition signatures from two-thirds of deed-holding homeowners matching County records.

The process to establish the SCBD was detailed, progressing through signature verification by the County SCBD Coordinator, legislative drafting, County Executive and County Council review, County Auditor review, published newspaper notices, a public hearing, and a final council vote (taking effect 45 days after County Executive signature). Proposed SCBD funds would cover common property maintenance (open space, recreation, entrance signs), insurance, loan repayment, legal fees, utilities, and permitted administrative costs. Because general administrative costs such as newsletters and website upkeep cannot be funded through an SCBD, SCCA would retain nominal dues. The proposed first-year charge would total $75 per household ($65 SCBD assessment + $10 SCCA administrative dues).

During the resident Q&A session, attendees discussed petition signature rules (every individual on the deed must sign), exit mechanisms (termination would likewise require a two-thirds homeowner petition and County approval), and assessment structures (no statutory cap, with ongoing budget input at quarterly meetings). In response to questions on startup and recurring costs, the Board discussed advertising the legislation for four weeks in a local paper and holding audits every four years. Board members also addressed maintenance and contracts, explaining that tree service pricing remains favorable and negotiated, trees fallen in common areas are left in place, and the $65 assessment plus $10 dues is projected to meet anticipated operating expenses.

Following the informational session, the regular Annual Meeting commenced. The minutes of the previous annual meeting were read and approved. The Treasurer presented a proposed budget of approximately $16,060 (projected based on 192 of 284 households contributing $75, plus $2,000 in additional donations). The Director's Report on architectural requests noted 2026 approvals for two fences, a front door paint color, and a backyard playset. The Board also noted correspondence with Mrs. Stancil regarding financial record requests, having provided readily available records and offering an in-person review.

Officer and director elections for the November 2026 through October 2028 term were conducted, with a quorum established by in-person attendees, directors, and absentee ballots. Frederick Rossmark was elected Treasurer with 108 votes. For the Board of Directors, Ed Maddox (101 votes), Jen Edwards (101 votes), and Judy Crawford (99 votes) received the highest vote counts and will be installed at the next meeting (write-in votes were recorded for Kevin Flaherty and Donald Donegan with 2 votes each). With no old or new business raised, the meeting adjourned at 8:39 p.m.

participants: Tyler Schulmeister, Jen Edwards, Ike Eichenlaub, Rebecca Blashack, Jim Guilfoyle, Ed Maddox, Dan Giles
content:
The Board discussed a Shipley’s Choice resident who is making landscaping changes on SCCA property without permission from the Board of Directors. Jim and Ike have informed him that he cannot make changes on SCCA property without permission from the Board. Yet he continues to make changes without permission. While many of his actions have resulted in favorable improvements, the Board has concerns about disruptions to utilities, potential impact on drainage and erosion, and other concerns. On August 4, a resident complained that Mr. Bradford was altering the landscape on SCCA property behind his house. Ike reported to the scene and observed Mr. Bradford removing a large tree. The Board voted unanimously to send Mr. Bradford another letter and if he persists in his unauthorized activities on SCCA property, the Board will pursue action through an attorney.

The current balance in the SCCA budget is $7982: $1464 is funds held for the playground and $5500 has been obligated for tree removal on three properties. The unobligated budget is $1018.

Membership on the Board was discussed. Rebecca, Ed, Jen and Mary’s two-year terms end this year. The Board agreed to pursue a new director for the vacant director position resulting from John Norville’s passing. Ike will assume recruiting and nominating responsibilities.

The County’s legal office has approved SCCA’s request to form a Special Community Benefit District for purposes of dues collection. A subcommittee comprised of Ike, Jim, Rebecca, Jen, Dan and Tyler will coordinate efforts to circulate a petition for 2/3 of Section 1 and 2 households to sign.

The annual in-person meeting will take place on Tuesday, October 20, 2026. The Board will hold an ad hoc video meeting on September 3, 2025.

Tyler discussed electricity brown-outs (temporary losses of electricity in households) and he suggested they seem to occur more frequently. Jim will contact BGE for information.

Ed inquired about asking the County to replace street lights in Shipley’s. Ike will contact the program manager who coordinated the traffic signal installation.

Jen suggested having a community forum on e-bike safety with information provided by AA County police. Jen will pursue a point of contact and Ike will follow-up with the police and the president of SCHOA for a potential collaborative meeting at the clubhouse.

participants: Tyler Schulmeister, Mary Kuhn, Jen Edwards, Ike Eichenlaub, Rebecca Blashack
content:
Three SCCA households brought dead trees to Jim and Ike’s attention. Jim and Ike are scheduled to assess the trees with a tree removal company on Tuesday, June 9.

A member of the SCCA community requested SCCA budget information and meeting minutes. The group agreed it’s in the community’s interest to make this information available. Ike will send meeting minutes to Tyler to post on the SCCA website. Budget information is already available in the annual newsletter.

Ike provided an update on SCCA’s efforts to establish a Special Taxing District for purposes of collecting dues. Ike last heard from Lori Blair, Deputy County Attorney, on the matter on April 21, at which time she indicated she was reviewing our request and would get back to Ike. She has not provided further information. Ike called Ms. Blair on Tuesday, June 2, and left a message; she has not responded. Ike will contact Council Member Fiedler on Monday, June 8, to ask for her support and intervention.

Rebecca informed the group she does not intend to serve as SCCA treasurer beyond her current term. The Board thanks Rebecca and is VERY sorry to see her leave the Board.

participants: Dan Giles, Tyler Schulmeister, Mary Kuhn, Jen Edwards, Ed Maddox, Ike Eichenlaub
content:
The Board agreed to send a letter to a SCCA community member, thanking him for his efforts on common area maintenance and stating he must contact the Board prior to making any changes on SCCA property.

The Board agreed to pay annual dues for membership in the Growth Action Network. The Board agreed not to pursue Pete Foley’s proposal to install cameras at the entrances to the neighborhood to monitor cars for crime prevention.

participants: Dan Giles, Neda Newnam, Tyler Schulmeister, Mary Kuhn, Jen Edwards, Ed Maddox, Ike Eichenlaub, Rebecca Blashack, Jim Guilfoyle
content:
Ike updated the group on the special taxing district initiative. He informed them he submitted documents to the County’s STD coordinator who in turn submitted our request to the County’s Law Office for review.

The Board voted in favor of regularly scheduled meetings to occur the first Thursday of every other month at 7:00 p.m., and agreed to schedule ad hoc meetings more frequently as needed.

There were no problems signing in to Google Meet for SCCA Board meeting purposes.

Mary and Jen mentioned the community has inquired about when the new traffic light will be activated and whether or not the crossing guard will remain after the light is activated. Ike has been posting information from the County’s project manager on SCCA’s website and Shipley’s Choice Facebook page.

participants: Jim Guilfoyle, Dan Giles, Neda Newnam, John Norville, Tyler Schulmeister, Mary Kuhn, Jen Edwards, Ed Maddox, Ike Eichenlaub, Rebecca Blashack
content:
The Board voted 9 to 1 in favor of pursuing a Special Community Benefits District for purposes of dues collection. Ike, Jim, Rebecca and Jen will serve on a committee to coordinate the application to the County.

Mary continues to submit paperwork for a playground grant from the County.
